body:
The fix proposed is not correct since in bootstrap correct markup uses `help-block`. I think we need to introduce another CSS class such as `activeform-error` and use it as a value for `yii\widgets\ActiveField::$errorOptions`.

The issue itself is valid.

Yes, bootstrap doesn't use `hint-block`. 

Does that mean `\yii\widgets\ActiveField` has to be corrected too? Because it has `public $hintOptions = ['class' => 'hint-block'];` ?
@samdark I think it's better we leave `yii\widgets\ActiveField` as is. With the current defaults, users can easily create a new set of styles based on bootstrap styles.
@qiangxue I don't agree. It's default behavior now and it's not correct.
Because it's semantical class and not visual one. It cannot conflict with another class like `help-block` does currently in bootstrap version of activeform.

Where is the conflict? This is just a default value that
- If you want to use bootstrap styles, it allows you to use it out-of-box.
- If you don't want to use bootstrap styles, you are free to override it with your own styles.

What's the benefit of introducing `activeform-error` without any support for it?
Agree with @qiangxue this should work using bootstrap styles without any additional styles.

Here: https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/blob/master/extensions/bootstrap/ActiveField.php#L328. Note that class is the same for both `hintOptions` and `errorOptions`. That makes our JavaScript code to change content of both tags on clientside validation error.
`yii\widgets\ActiveField` is OK. The issue is about bootstrap one.

I propose not touching visual part i.e. leave markup always as is. The change is that for error field we're adding additional class `error` or `error-block` and using `'class' => 'help-block error-block'` in bootstrap field class.
Suggest to solve this issue via data attributes like `data-placeholder="validation-error"`. Its not correct to solve this issue through additional css classes.
I think `'class' => 'help-block help-block-error'` matches bootstrap naming pretty well.
After talking with @samdark via Skype i think good idea is 'class' => 'help-block help-block-error'. This is bootstrap way. Similar to 'btn btn-primary', etc
